content: Benjamin Hutchison Humble, M.B.E., resided in Arrochar from 1960 to 1970. He was a highly productive author and a distinguished Scottish climber, credited with the establishment of the modern Scottish Mountain Rescue teams. In addition to his mountaineering achievements, he was an avid photographer and filmmaker. Ben Humble was born in Dumbarton in 1903, one of the sons of the manager of Dennystown Forge. Despite being completely deaf, he pursued a career in dentistry and later contributed to advancements in forensic dentistry. His deafness, however, made him somewhat irritable in his interactions with others. A particular incident involved the publication of an unflattering photograph of him, humorously referred to as the Humble Kipper, which depicted him at breakfast. This incident led to him refusing to speak to the photographer for a decade. For more comprehensive information, refer to the detailed biography of Ben Humble available on the Arrochar, Tarbet, and Ardlui Heritage Group website. He passed away in 1977.
